results.content:
Hey Product Hunt, Praney here. I build Vois solo from Melbourne.  
  
Since the first Vois launch here, one complaint kept coming back from  
podcasters and narrators, and I had it myself: cloud voice tools charge per  
character, so every retake of the same paragraph costs money again. I  
started calling it the preview tax. You stop iterating, and the read stays  
mediocre.  
  
Vois 2.x is my answer: an ElevenLabs alternative that runs on your own  
machine. Every subscription has unlimited generation: no tokens, no usage  
meter. Retake a paragraph fifty times and your bill does not move.  
  
What is in 2.x:  
  
- Four engines, picked per job: Fast for drafts (about 3x real time on CPU,  
about 6x with GPU acceleration on Apple Silicon), Expressive for [...] This is the 2nd launch from Vois. View more

ElevenLabs plays a different role in the audio stack: it’s the go-to alternative when the priority is generating lifelike speech, not just transcribing it. Whisper by OpenAI is excellent for ASR, but it doesn’t solve the “voice output” problem; ElevenLabs fills that gap with premium text-to-speech and voice cloning designed for customer-facing experiences.

The key differentiator is realism and expressiveness, which matters for narration, branded voices, and conversational agents that need natural pacing and emotion. Voice cloning makes it possible to create consistent, recognizable voices quickly, which is hard to replicate with more generic TTS systems. [...] ElevenLabs also offers workflows that feel like editing a script rather than recording takes, helping teams iterate on voiceovers fast. For product teams, the API-first approach can make it straightforward to embed speech generation into apps, prototypes, and content pipelines.

Trade-offs to be aware of include consistency over long-form output and extra care needed around numbers, abbreviations, and symbols. For teams prioritizing premium voice quality and speed of iteration, those constraints are often manageable compared with the lift of building comparable TTS in-house.

results.title: ElevenLabs Reviews (2026) | Product Hunt
results.content:
❗ Extremely disappointing — feels like a scam. This was my first time trying to create an audiobook, and I honestly believed ElevenLabs would be a reliable platform. I subscribed to what was clearly labeled as a monthly plan, not a credit-based plan. But after signing up, I was shocked to find that the system actually uses credits, not unlimited monthly usage as advertised. I created about 10 short voices, which used around 3,000 credits — fine. But just a few hours later, when I made only two voices slightly over two minutes each, the system deducted 50,000 credits — half of my entire balance (100,000). I immediately contacted support. They said they would reply within 48 hours, but I never received a single response. The pricing is deceptive, the system is unclear, and the customer [...] Promoted
